instruction:
Parse this JSON log line and return a JSON object with ts, level, msg and trace_id only:
{"ts": "2023-10-12T14:05:07Z", "level": "error", "msg": "payment failed", "user_id": 4821, "trace_id": "abc123"}

Flatten this nested JSON log into a single level using dot notation as JSON:
{"event": "login", "context": {"user": {"id": 7, "name": "alice"}, "ip": "10.0.0.5"}}

Extract the value at the path request.user.id from this JSON log as JSON with just that value:
{"request": {"user": {"id": 991, "role": "admin"}, "path": "/admin"}, "status": 200}

This JSON log embeds an exception object. Return JSON with exception_type, exception_message and the first stack line:
{"ts": "2023-10-12T14:06:00Z", "level": "error", "msg": "handler crashed", "exception": {"type": "ValueError", "message": "invalid amount", "stack": ["  at charge(/app/billing.py:44)", "  at main(/app/main.py:10)"]}}

This JSON log stores the time as epoch milliseconds. Convert it to an ISO 8601 UTC string and return JSON with time_iso and level:
{"time": 1697129107123, "level": "warn", "msg": "cache miss rate high"}

Normalize the level field of this JSON log: map warn to warning. Return the normalized JSON object:
{"ts": "2023-10-12T14:07:00Z", "level": "warn", "msg": "slow query", "duration_ms": 1450}

This JSON log has a tags array. Promote each tag into a boolean field of the same name and return the resulting JSON object:
{"msg": "deploy finished", "tags": ["canary", "eu-west"], "level": "info"}
Write a Python snippet that parses one JSON log line with json.loads and returns an empty dict instead of raising when the line is malformed

This JSON document contains an array of events. Return JSON with event_count and the names of the events as an array:
{"received_at": "2023-10-12T14:08:00Z", "events": [{"name": "signup", "user": 1}, {"name": "purchase", "user": 2}, {"name": "refund", "user": 2}]}

Flatten the http object of this JSON log into top level status_code and path fields and return the full object as JSON:
{"ts": "2023-10-12T14:08:30Z", "level": "error", "http": {"status": 500, "path": "/api/orders", "latency_ms": 91}}

This log line looks like JSON but has a trailing comma. Report whether it parses and why not as JSON:
{"ts": "2023-10-12T14:09:00Z", "level": "info", "msg": "hello",}

Parse this Graylog GELF JSON log and map the numeric level 4 to its name. Return JSON with host, level and short_message:
{"version": "1.1", "host": "web01", "short_message": "disk usage above 90 percent", "level": 4, "timestamp": 1697129107}

This JSON log stores epoch seconds. Convert the timestamp to an ISO 8601 UTC string and return JSON:
{"timestamp": 1697129107, "level": "info", "msg": "job finished"}

Extract the params object from this JSON log as JSON:
{"level": "info", "msg": "search", "params": {"q": "prometheus", "page": 2, "limit": 10}}

Build a JSON log line from these field values with keys ts, level, service and msg (no extra fields):
level=info, service=checkout, msg=order created, ts=2023-10-12T14:10:00Z
